items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: Tom Thumb was very popular then... this guy -- what I was saying, he was an attraction to the Hotcha Hot Shot Club because people like to come there just to see him, you know.

ctx.x: This owner, this new owner -- he had bought the old Hacha Not-Shot Club, see, and turned it into a night club -- well, it was like a place of pleasure, see. Like, it had a gaming room, you know, and refreshments, and naturally it was very - how can you say -- I'll say an overwhelming place, you know, something like they have a place similar to it now, this Hawaii Kai. It's up there by the Winter Garden, Maha Key,

you see, on Broadway, across from the Urus and the Circle Theater. What is that -- I think -- theatrical -- it's right where the Capital Theater used to be, somewhere near the Ma Kellinger Theater there, you know. The Hot Shot Club used to resemble that place, the Hawaii Kai, you see. In fact, they got one of the performers that used to be in the original Hotcha Hot Shot Club -- he was in the show, you know, and he was an attraction, see, because they didn't what he was. They thought he was -- see, Tom Thumb was…

Monarchy, which they called a tour -- that was like touring the world, you see. Like you're going around the world -- they call that monarchy, see. And they wanted to make sure that everyone was enjoying their pleasures, you see, because society was more gigantic. I think society became anemic after that (unintelligible) these things -- Because I don't think that the Board of Health actually realized what was occurring, you know. By the time when they find it out, you know, they got the condemnation sign up…
